items.description: Pixel-space diffusion models have recently re-emerged as a compelling alternative to latent diffusion, avoiding the lossy latent bottleneck and separately trained autoencoder. JiT shows that a vanilla diffusion transformer can generate directly in pixel space by replacing the commonly used velocity prediction ($\boldsymbol{u}$-prediction) with clean image prediction ($\boldsymbol{x_0}$-prediction). items.name: Behavioral Couplings: From Formation to Behavioral Emergence in Language Models
items.title: Behavioral Couplings: From Formation to Behavioral Emergence in Language Models
items.description: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) can induce behaviors beyond those explicitly targeted. For example, training a model to respond more warmly can make it more sycophantic, and training it to write insecure code can cause broad misalignment on prompts unrelated to coding. items.name: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
items.title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
items.description: Reproducible and analytically robust research findings are essential to scientific progress, but evaluating these properties typically requires costly manual effort. We investigate whether LLM agents can help automate reproduction and robustness analysis, using a medical case study grounded in the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database, a widely used U.S. cancer registry underlying tens of thousands of published studies. items.title: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses
items.description: Scientific discovery requires developing worthwhile hypotheses into practical investigations, yet learning from this evolving research process remains challenging. We introduce an operational definition of valuable and testable research hypotheses: evidence-grounded claims about consequential uncertainties, coupled with feasible investigations, explicit decision criteria, and alternative explanations. items.title: Task-aligned spectral inductive biases in parameterized quantum circuits
items.description: Parameterized quantum circuits are widely investigated in quantum machine learning, yet how their architecture can provide task-aligned inductive biases remains poorly understood. items.name: Beyond the Answer: Student-Conditioned Trace Construction for Reasoning Distillation
items.title: Beyond the Answer: Student-Conditioned Trace Construction for Reasoning Distillation
items.description: A reasoning trace can accompany a correct answer without providing effective supervision for a particular student. We study how to construct traces that improve learning beyond answer-only supervision by considering both their intermediate content and their accessibility to the target learner. items.title: Waiting Buys Exactly Two Moments: Endogenous Identification in Prediction-Driven Allocation

items.title: Quality-of-Transmission Estimation in Quantum Networks: Compute, Simulate, or Learn?
items.description: Future quantum networks will rely on control-plane decisions such as routing, scheduling, entanglement provisioning, purification, and memory allocation. Each decision depends on a timely and reliable estimate of the quality of the entanglement that a candidate path can deliver, with end-to-end fidelity as a central metric. items.name: Self-Building Labs
items.title: Self-Building Labs
items.description: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) accelerate scientific discovery by automating experimental execution and optimization. AI agents can increasingly propose new experiments, but existing SDLs can only run the procedures they were built for. Adapting them to a new experiment still takes extensive manual engineering, which makes laboratory flexibility the bottleneck for scaling discovery. items.name: CocoRNA: Collective RNA Design with Cooperative Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
items.title: CocoRNA: Collective RNA Design with Cooperative Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Designing RNA sequences that reliably fold into specific secondary structures is essential for understanding their biological functions but remains a challenging computational problem. We propose CocoRNA, a cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for RNA inverse design. items.title: Acceptance Is Not Speed: Length Inflation in Training-Free Lossy Speculative Decoding
items.description: Speculative decoding typically characterizes speedup by draft tokens accepted per verification round. Lossless verification preserves the target model's output distribution and thus expected completion length, making this metric a meaningful efficiency proxy. items.title: Learning Personalized Memory Gating from Delayed One-Sided Feedback
items.description: Long-term memory enables language-model agents to personalize future interactions, but a finite memory bank cannot preserve every extracted fact. Existing memory gating policies are typically shared across users and therefore fail to account for user-specific patterns of future reuse. In this paper, we study memory gating at the fact level. items.title: Explainable Machine Learning Analysis of Temperature Effects on Mechanical Strength of Fiber-Reinforced High-Performance Concrete
items.description: Predicting the compressive strength of fiber-reinforced high-performance concrete subjected to temperature exposure is challenging because to the intricate interdependencies of mixture composition, fiber properties, curing conditions, and temperature. items.title: Steering beyond Language: Improving Multilingual Training-Free Text Embeddings via Paired-Residual Subspace Removal
items.description: While deriving text embeddings directly from frozen LLMs has emerged as a promising direction, existing methods focus almost exclusively on English, leaving multilingual settings largely unexplored. items.title: Beyond SAEs: Consistent Concept Discovery with Sparse Coding
items.description: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) explain foundation model representations by decomposing activations into sparse combinations of learned dictionary atoms. items.title: FuTransformer: FP8 prefill and INT4 decode for Llama-style inference on Hopper

items.title: DrugHarness: An Evolvable Agent Harness for Computational Drug Discovery
items.description: Computational drug discovery requires agents to compose scientific operations and adapt to changing evidence and constraints. items.title: Universal Semantic Enhancement for Weakly Supervised Anomaly Detection
items.description: Weakly supervised anomaly detection on tabular data is an essential task in many label-scarce applications, since tabular data is widely encountered and it is commonly observed in practice that only a limited number of labeled anomalies are available alongside abundant unlabeled samples. items.title: The Italian lawmaking process: a unified and structured dataset
items.description: The Italian legislative process is documented in detailed parliamentary records hosted in institutional websites.
